claim: An AWS access portal (user interactive) session lasts for the duration configured in IAM Identity Center, which can be up to 90 days; it ends when the user signs out or an administrator ends it.
question: How long can an IAM Identity Center user interactive (AWS access portal) session last?

qualifiers.condition: duration is configured by the administrator

evidence.quote: User interactive sessions can last for the duration configured in IAM Identity Center, which can be up to 90 days.
They end when the user signs out or when an administrator ends their session.

note: d005 (maximum). Default value: see user-interactive-sessions page. d010: the 7 to 90 days change of 2023-09-12 is only in a What's New post that robots.txt refuses; no history row.

claim: Application sessions with AWS managed applications have a one hour lifetime by default and are refreshed automatically while the user interactive session is valid; after the user interactive session ends, they end at their next refresh, typically within 30 minutes.
question: How long do IAM Identity Center application sessions last, and how fast do they end after sign-out?

evidence.quote: By default, application sessions have a one hour lifetime, but they're automatically refreshed as long as the underlying user interactive session remains valid. This refresh mechanism provides a seamless experience for users while maintaining security controls. When a user interactive session ends, either through user sign-out or administrator action, the application sessions will end at their next refresh attempt, typically within 30 minutes.

claim: IAM role sessions created from a permission set operate independently once established: they last for the duration configured in the permission set, up to 12 hours, regardless of the status of the original sign-in session.
question: Does signing out of, or disabling a user in, IAM Identity Center end the user's existing IAM role sessions in AWS accounts?

values.display: regardless of the status of the original sign-in session

qualifiers.condition: duration set in the permission set

evidence.quote: Unlike application sessions, IAM role sessions operate independently once established. They persist for the duration configured in the permission set (or IAM role when using account access manager), which can be up to 12 hours, regardless of the status of the original sign-in session.

note: Exam trap: to cut access at once you must also revoke the role sessions; disabling the user is not enough.

claim: When a user's access is disabled, the user loses IAM Identity Center access and cannot create new application sessions immediately, loses existing application sessions within 30 minutes, and loses existing AWS account sessions within 12 hours or less, depending on the permission set session duration.
question: How quickly does a disabled IAM Identity Center user lose access to portal, application and AWS account sessions?

evidence.quote: | User's access disabled | Effective immediately | Effective immediately | Within 30 minutes | Within 12 hours or less. Duration depends on IAM role session expiry duration configured for the permission set (or IAM role when using account access manager). |
evidence.table_header: | Action | User loses IAM Identity Center access | User can't create new application sessions | User can't access existing application sessions | User loses access to existing AWS account sessions |
